title: The Missing Primitive for Agent Swarms — Lou Bichard, Ona
talk_summary: Lou Bichard (Ona) argues that for agent 'software factories' the runtime, orchestration, and triggers are largely solved, but the missing primitive is a coordination layer — because GitHub/Linear are human tools that get noisy with many agents. He proposes encoding the SDLC as explicit micro-steps/state machines with durable execution and a CLI gate that agents must call to prove a stage is done before proceeding.

takeaways.technique: Explicit SDLC micro-step state machine instead of coarse stages
takeaways.what_they_do: Break the coarse 5-step SDLC into deterministic micro-steps and drive agents through them as a state machine/workflow rather than letting them interpret 'plan' or 'test' loosely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to find ways to actually break down the SDLC into these some of these micro steps ... do them in sort of deterministic ways

takeaways.what_they_do: Ship a CLI the local agent must invoke to ask 'have I achieved this SDLC stage, can I proceed?' — a programmatic gate rather than reading GitHub state.

takeaways.technique: Don't use GitHub/Linear as the agent coordination layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats PR/ticket tools as noisy human interfaces; coordination (task pickup, handoff, intervention points) needs a dedicated layer so humans can see where to step in.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GitHub is not a coordination layer for agents. It gets incredibly overwhelming ... incredibly noisy for you as a human to make sense of where you should step in

takeaways.technique: Harness engineering: encode process into the repo
takeaways.what_they_do: Everything in the repo that gives the agent feedback — skills, agents.md, unit tests — is 'harness'; when an agent gets lost, encode that lesson back into the repo/context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: figuring out where the agents gets lost and then encoding that knowledge back into your repository or context again

takeaways.technique: Parent-controller with isolated sub-agents and message passing
takeaways.what_they_do: A controlling parent agent spawns sub-agents (in separate VMs or processes), gives each a small slice of context and one task, and they message results back to the parent which governs the whole task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the parent is the the controlling agent and the sub-agents obviously then are given small bits of contact, individual tasks to complete and then will do message passing back

takeaways.technique: VM-level isolation for bursty agent builds
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues containers aren't a sufficient security boundary and cause noisy-neighbor compute contention; full VMs give isolation and predictable resources for bursty coding agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a container is not bulletproof isolation boundary ... They're also bursty ... you have noisy neighbor problems
